notes.title: Sinking Simulator: Legacy
notes.content:
I'm happy to announce the release of Sinking Simulator: Legacy

This is the old 2013 version with a few minor additions. Notably the material table and ships updated/designed exclusively for this build.

[b]You can buy the game  [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2367960/Sinking_Simulator_Legacy/]Here[/url][/b]

Sinking Simulator: Legacy is meant to help revive Sinking Simulator and possibly spawn more.
Turning Sinking Simulator into a paid game helped me tremendously, but it wasn't quite enough to keep the game running.

I do not expect the Legacy game to be as successful as Sinking Simulator, but I remain hopeful.

There will be a few minor updates to the Legacy edition, primarily bug fixes and Quality of Life things.
But outside of this, [u][b]this version of the game is not meant to be in active development.
[/b][/u]
Meaning I have no plan to update it beyond what will be coming over in the next couple of days/weeks.

However, Good news if you are a skilled programmer.
[b]This game is also open source.[/b]
You can look up the Source Code on Github  [url=https://github.com/Wren6991/Ship-Sandbox]Here[/url]

This means, if you're interested to create your own branch with your own features, go for it!
This is effectively what happened with [b]"Floating Sandbox"[/b]
Floating Sandbox is a different build which was originally based on Sinking Simulator
It has evolved a lot since then.

I strongly suggest you check it out if you like this kind of games
[url=https://gamejolt.com/games/floating-sandbox/353572]Floating Sandbox[/url]

[b]Please, keep in mind![/b]
"Sinking Simulator" is a protected [b]US Trademark.[/b]
I strongly advice you avoid using this name if you wish to create your own variant.

I've also been thinking about creating a "Community edition" where the community can update the game themselves and share some of the revenues.
However, I'm not quite sure how to do it at the moment.

This is all for now.
Thank you all for your support!

notes.title: So... What happened?
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone,[/b]

Long time no see.

I've been thinking about making this announcement for a while but I wasn't sure how to do it.
I figured I'd be straight to the point

[h3]What happened?[/h3]

Well... We had plans for a few updates down the line back in early 2020, Unfortunately, I'm sure you all know what happened that year...

Since the game has been Free we didn't really make any profit.
This means, once the Pandemic started and we were in Lockdown, we had to change our priorities...
Paying rent, food, etc..  life isn't cheap.

Any time spent working on the game would not return any significant income, (that's including the support pack DLC)

Hence, Sinking Simulator has been in Limbo ever since.

[h3]What now?[/h3]

It's hard to say.
Fred is the sole programmer for the game and now he's way too busy with work

There may be minor updates coming up, however we can't make any promises. 
The fate of the game is currently unknown.

[h3]What else?[/h3]

Well, there's one thing I'm going to try, but I'm unsure if it's a good idea or not.
I've said many time before I didn't want to put a price tag on the game

However, now the economy is.. going wild.
I have a full time Job, so I've been able to do "fine" for the past 2 years, but it started to get rough lately.

I've discussed the idea with Fred to see what he thought.
We agreed if we were to put a price on the game it ought to be under 1$
Though, the minimum price I was able to set was 0.99$ 

I've contacted Valve to start this process,
I've been told it was permanent, once it is done, it cannot be reverted back

[h3]Why?[/h3]

Primarily because as I've said, on my end, things are getting tougher than usual.

If we're lucky, that money may be used to update the game,
However this is a big "IF"

Over 500K people currently owns the game on Steam and due to the lack of updates every months there are fewer people getting it.

Plus, now that the game will cost 1$ it will likely drop further.
For now, hopefully this will help rounding up the months. (paying bills, debts, etc...)

I'd like to be optimistic and say that everything will be alright, but in truth, I have absolutely no idea what will happen.

I'm sure it will upset a few people and I can't blame them
Fortunately, if you currently own a free copy of the game you won't have to pay.

I'm also considering the idea of creating Steam Cards
However there's one big problem. 
The cards are not compatible with the free copy

Meaning, half a million people won't be able to use them.
So that's kind of useless. 

[h3]Can you release the Source Code?[/h3]
I've been discussing this idea with Fred, 
So far we're not sure.  
Maybe some day, but there's no guarantee 

I've been considering turning the Game into a community driven project where people can contribute and add their own features.
Nothing's official yet.

[h3]What about Floating Sandbox?[/h3]

It's a nice game originally based on the old Sinking Sim from 2013
It has been entirely reworked and I'm really happy Gabriele managed to pull this off

I do strongly recommend you look it up, especially if your computer cannot handle Sinking Simulator too well.
[url=https://gamejolt.com/games/floating-sandbox/353572][/url]

To be honest, 
I'd love to see more games like it.
Sinking Simulator will be 10 years old next year.
It has millions of views on YouTube and sparkled countless discussions.

This alone makes me very happy.

Thank you all ❤

notes.title: MULTI-LAYERS & THE ROUTE TO BETTER COLLISIONS
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

For quite some time, we’ve been discussing potential ways to improve the game’s collision while remaining simple enough to allow complex designs.

For the sake of simplicity and helping you folks visualize what I mean, I’ve used the software “Algodoo” in order to demonstrate the idea using a similar system.
You can download it here : http://www.algodoo.com/

We believe we’ve found an elegant solution to this issue and it is by using a “Multi-Layered” system.
Essentially, it means, most aspects of the creations will be simulated on different layers.
For instance, you could have the Hull of a ship as a different layer than the background “non hull” 
Since the hull would be on a different layer, it will be treated as a different entity and it won’t be subject to the same amount of force as the background “non hull” of the ship.
It means we could (in theory) properly simulate Water pressure as the inside of this new Hull layer would be empty, (as opposed to the usual ships that use the background “non hull” to fill the space).

Using the Hull on a new layer would also allow some types of interactivity that weren’t possible before. 
For instance, If the weight of water inside the ship is properly simulated, it could exert stress on the hull leading to structural failure and collapse. 

It would also allow the creations of new Tools that only interact with a given layer.
This means we could destroy only the hull while keeping the background intact
This isn’t possible right now because it would cut the ship in 2. While cutting only the Hull would allow the ships to keep their structural integrity and of course, expose the inside to the sea water

[img]https://i.imgur.com/uYjCLi8.gif[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9ikMbIG.gif[/img]


[u][b][h3]What else can be done with Layers?[/h3][/b][/u]

Layers will open entire new ranges of possibilities for the creation of various contraptions and complex structures.
However, for that to be possible we need to introduce new features “constraints” to the game

Constraints are features for ship builders that will allow them to constraint layers together in multiple ways

[b]Axis:[/b] The Axis will create a point between 2 or more layers that will only allow rotating motion
[img]https://i.imgur.com/rTRTMFF.gif[/img]

[b]Weld:[/b] The Weld is like the Axis, with the exception no movements are allowed between the points
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Ti64Sov.gif[/img]

[b]Rail:[/b] The Rail will use 2 points and allow 2 or more layers to move in a linear motion between them. 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/YZfWSsO.gif[/img]

[b]Motor:[/b] A motor is essentially like the Axis with the exception it applies torque in the desired direction.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/fR2SLg3.gif[/img]

Combining those features together can lead to some amazing creations.
For instance, you could make a drawbridge, a piston, an engine, etc…
Near limitless amount of new possibilities.

[u][b][h3]What about collisions?[/h3][/b][/u]

Self Collision is something we wanted to include from the start, however it’s quite complicated to do properly
Though, This multi-layer system won’t necessarily help simplifying collisions, It will however, create the potential for a much better system.

Right now, the idea is to keep each layer independent of one another, meaning they won’t collide with each other. But layers with the same ID will.

Since we want to move the Hull to a different layer than the background (non hull)
It will allow players to drop a heavy object on top of a ship and pierce through the entire ship without cutting the ship in half. Instead it will just punch its way through the hull layer and expose the bottom to the sea water.

Though, the Hull layer won’t be completely independent of the background layer
Otherwise both would end up separating and that’s bad. We don’t want them to float away from each other.
Therefore, the Background will need to act like a support for the hull and vice versa.

[u][b][h3]What about loading the ships?[/h3][/b][/u]

Due to the increase in complexity, we believe the best and simplest way to load a complex creation is to simply ZIP it with a Json file targeting each part of the creation.
The game would then load the zip file and of course upload it on the steam workshop

However, it is also likely the game will include a Ship Editor to make the whole creation much simpler.  This way it may be possible to create things that would not be possible by converting image as images are limited by the pixels and it starts to get very complicated when we have many layers and potential interaction between them.

notes.title: Real Fake Lights
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

Fred has been hard at work and managed to get a new "Fake" Lighting system into the game
This is an update to the Testing Branch.
It will become public in a few days if there aren't any major issues.


[h2]What is a fake lighting system?[/h2]
Essentially, this is a Shader which change the appearance of the texture based on ambient light. They also support all colours

We have 2 shaders

[olist]
[*] [u][b][h3]exlights[/h3][/b][/u]
The colour value will change the appearance of the texture layer.
a White value will make the texture just as bright as if would be in daytime
A black value would make it just as dark as everything else around. 
It is very useful if you plan to create some sort of interior texture where you want the inside of the ships to remain visible. example below
[img]https://i.imgur.com/WKjbW9F.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/oF4U4HX.png[/img]

[*][u][b][h3]inlights[/h3][/b][/u]
inlight will essentially replace the texture itself and can get much brighter than what it may look light in daytime
It is very useful if you want to make an exterior texture where the porthole are very bright at night,
[img]https://i.imgur.com/SS0nIfk.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/JERNaBw.png[/img]
[/olist]


This is what the layer looks like
[img]https://i.imgur.com/LRkQHPg.png[/img]

The black background essentially means there's nothing to change
You can create your own in the same way you create textures.

There is no way to toggle it off at the moment
so if you wish to have a dark version of the ship at night, I strongly recommend you create a layer without those fake lights added in. 


[img]https://i.imgur.com/89wuA82.png[/img]

notes.title: NPC Ideas
notes.content:
[b][h1]NPC Idea[/h1][/b]
Hello everyone!, 
I wanted to let you know our current Idea for the potential implementations of NPCs into the game. 
[b]The following is mostly Hypothetical, it doesn't mean the final result will happen nor could it be exactly as described below, [/b]
----------------------------------

By using the multi layer system I thought it would be good to create some sort of NPC character and Nodes
The nodes would really just be a simple colored paths in it's own layer, using color coded nodes would allow the creation of zones and specific "behaviors" in each and used as the pathway of the NPC inside the ships

the amount of NPC types could be controllable in the toolbox
the NPCs would be a sprite character (most likely a very simple shape like a stick figure) they would be scalable in the toolbox so they can be the right size for the ships.
Their default size would be 1.8 pixels in height with a possible variation up to 0.05 on either sides in order to give a bit of varieties
[h2]NPC TYPES[/h2]

[u][b]Crew members / Staff[/b][/u]
White or light grey in colour, they have access to every zone

[u][b]Passenger & Class[/b][/u]
Dark grey or black in colour, they can move only in their appropriate class level and the one below them

[u][b]Engineers[/b][/u]
Dark red in colour, they can only travel in the Staff only areas

[u][b]VIP[/b][/u]
Custom NPC, They can go anywhere, possibility of giving it a name tag, can be any colour (default blue)
We can also make a list of randomly generated names and take in the names submitted by people who donate 5$ or more (conditions apply)
[h3]NPC Appearance[/h3]
We can use sprites of various kinds to show the NPCs in the game. Here are a few  simple designs I have made in about a minute. They can of course be more complex
[img]https://i.imgur.com/S59t7nf.png[/img]
[h2]ZONES[/h2]
[h3]lifeboats[/h3][list]
[*] this zone is accessible only when the alarm is triggered (custom button in the toolbox or any of the menus)
[*] All NPC types will try to reach the zone, Priority by class type (can be toggled off)
[*] Each pixel can contain up to 16 NPC , it takes 10 seconds (or manually triggered) for NPC to trigger the Lifeboats and be safe  (disappearing , possibly adding a counter for a survivor stats
[*] Lifeboats will not deploy on their own if the passenger count is below half (8), Players can always manually override it and deploy them at any moment 
[*] Possibility of spawning a Lifeboat Sprite/particle when it is deployed, if so, then it could be designed by the players[/list]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/KaPCKza.png[/img]
[h3]Passenger, Class[/h3]
3 different colours for 3 different permissions level, 1 2 and 3 for the class, it can be toggled off to disable class restriction
NPC will pass most of their time in their respective areas
[h3]Staff only[/h3]
Areas accessible only to the staff/crew of the vessel
[h3]Hole[/h3]
[list][*] This “zone” is automatically generated when the ship has any sort of structural failure,
It is created only around the parts of the structure that are exposed to “air” with the exception of the natural/intended edges of the ships
[*] If a NPC enter this zone, the NPC “Falls” off the structure right into the open sea or it is added to the Death count
[*] Staff NPC may be able to perform small repairs to the structure [/list]
[h3]AI BEHAVRIORS[/h3]
[list][*]All Npc just moves in a pseudo random direction following the nodes they are linked to unless they commanded otherwise (emergency AI override)
[*]All Npc will die "drown" once they are underwater for more than 15 seconds
[*]All Npc will die if they float in the sea for more than 1 minute or if the temperature is above 100°C, (could be timed as well, the “survivability time” would be inversely linear to the temperature  for instance, at 50°C it’s 1 minute, at 100°C it’s 10 seconds
[*]All Npc (except Engineers) avoid water, if possible using Pathfinding on their nodes
Engineers will try to repair the structure in their path, they will actively seek to put down Fire with the help of Staff
[*]If the alarm is on, NPC will ignore Class/zone restriction in order to reach safety.
[*]If there is no lifeboat available (or in reach) NPC will move to the farthest point away from water
[*]No NPC can pass through the hull materials. Hence it is important for ships to have a proper interior design that facilitate their movements[/list]

[h2]TOOLS[/h2]
[h3]Add NPC[/h3]
Creates NPC using the left mouse click (can also remove the NPC using the right click or a bind such as Shift + Left click )
[h3]Kill NPC[/h3]
Removes NPC from the ships but adds them to the Death counter
[h3]Alarm[/h3]
Turns on/off the alarm and reset NPC behaviors  (If Logic gates are implemented, the Alarm could be toggled by them)
[h3]Streaming Integration[/h3]
An integration to the major streaming platforms allowing views interaction with the game. For instance, naming NPC after themselves or creating live Polls
[h2]Stats[/h2]
[list][*]Total count of NPC onboards,  possibly counting each class as well
[*]Death count, (restarts when reloading or changing ships)
[*]Safe count for all NPC that have reached safety
[*]Secret Death count - A death count that doesn’t reset until the game is closed, (accessible using the dev tools)
[*]Each NPC can have their own name and Biography, they can be changed at will by the player, However, by default, we can use a random name generator and possibly add permanently the name of Patreon Supporters and potentially others
[/list]

If Achievement can be implemented, those stats could be used to unlock some
For instance, the achievement “A night to remember”  could be triggered when the death count reach at least or exactly 1517 people while playing on the night settings

notes.title: Patreon?
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello everyone[/b][/h1]

I will try to make this short
This post is here for me to ask the community if you guys think we should make a Patreon page.

It was often suggested by multiple people over the last few years but I always refused under the principle that I don't like to lock content behind a paywall and the lack of proper organisation.

Not only that, but the game is being worked on as a hobby. 
We both have jobs taking our time, so a Patreon would just feel weird given our context.
Aka, our livelihood do not depend on the success of the game, which nowadays appears to be a pretty rare thing among Game dev or youtube/streaming platforms etc... 

This is why I make this post.  I personally started thinking about it more and more in the last month or so.  I thought about potential ways to maybe make it work, but it depends on the community.

Hence I want to make a poll. 

Should we start a Patreon page to support the development of Sinking Simulator?
Here's a link to the Poll
https://www.strawpoll.me/19141586

of course, I cannot promise regular game updates. it really depends on the kind of content being worked on at the time and Fred's schedule.

[h3]What would Patrons get? [/h3]
[olist]
[*] Access to experimental builds before being pushed to steam
[*] A Unique role on our Discord Server
[*] Better look at the future plans of the game
[*] Access to the original files and give suggestions for revisions (commissioned works)
[*] Permanent name in the game credits
[/olist]

That's really about it. 
I can't really think of anything else of value which wouldn't go against my "no paywall" policies 
I also have to look more in depth to Patreon's policies before making any promises

[h3]Please take note,[/h3] 
The purpose of those experimental builds are for play testing before we update the Steam Branch.  

they will vary from update to update and they may be unstable. 
We won't deliberately delay the steam update to favorise Patreons. 
We'll just dump stuff there for people to look at it if they are interested. 

We're also open to suggestion.

notes.title: Over 100'000 Downloads & Asking the community about Merchs
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello everyone! [/b][/h1] 
This is our First Milestone on Steam,  
In just over 1 month and a half, we've "sold" over [u][b]100'000[/b][/u] copies of Sinking Simulator
Many thanks to all of you folks.

The game has been available for years on other platforms such as IndieDB and Gamejolts
If we combine all of the platforms together we get very close to 1 Millions total downloads in the past 4 years.

This is incredible.  It is even more incredible knowing we've never spend a dime on any sort of advertisements. It is completely community driven.  So I wanted to thanks all of you for your support


[u][h1][b]Merchandise[/b][/h1][/u] 
It has been suggested to me a couple of time over the years and I am seriously considering the idea.

I wanted to know if people here would be interested by Merchandise themed around Sinking Simulator

Right now, I have a Poll running [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/65465468/community?view_as=subscriber] on my Youtube Channel[/url]

Recently, I have been streaming a bit more than usual. I've noticed the Software I use for Streaming "Streamlabs OBS" has tools to setup a Merch store.
Of course, it is not free. It requires me to pay for their premium membership which comes at about 12$ a month (yearly payment, so it's about 144$)

Hence why I wonder if it is worth it.

If it ends up overwhelmingly positive, I will allocate some of the DLC profits to commissions a bunch of Custom Designs and Artworks Exclusive to the Merch Store

In the latest post :[url=https://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791465465604/announcements/detail/1727624178338793499]DLC And Policies[/url]

I've said the money made by the sales of the DLC will be used exclusively for improving the game. However it doesn't apply for the merchs. 
The profit from Merch won't be strictly directed toward the game

I will kick start the first year using money from my own pocket.
But then I must make sure the profit that comes out of those are at a minimum paying for the yearly hosting/prime fees and potentially extending it over time if it is favourable 

(I am specifying this in order to avoid any sort of confusion.)
I will do my best to remain as transparent as possible.
I do not intent to pay for a second year out of my own pocket. 
[u]If the project fails, then it may never come back again[/u]

notes.title: Sinking Simulator, DLCs and Updates
notes.content:
Hello everyone, I wanted to talk about our views and politics on DLCs 

First, I need you guys to understand one thing. The development of this game is essentially a Hobby. 
It is not a full time project and it just cannot be a full time project as the market is not strong enough. 

We've also decided to keep the game free for the simple fact if people had to pay for it, they'd have a higher expectation, both for quality and for more regular kind of updates

[h1]What are the DLCs about?[/h1]
We want to add new features into the game, but as previously said, Fred is essentially the only person actively working on the game and it is a hobby. 
Me on the other hand, my job is to spread the word, to keep in touch with the community, Fred doesn't have time for that either.  We both have full time jobs 

This is why we have come up with the DLCs.  They are there for people who want to see more content added to the game,  Content that may not be easily done or perhaps content that would take a long time to implement.  They will allow us to afford content that wouldn't be available for free, like License or commissions, etc...

[h1] DLCs Politics [/h1]
We do not want to lock content behind a pay wall, we believe this is a hostile practice by the industry in order to milk more money from their customers. 
For us, DLCs are extra content that can be downloaded which is not necessary to the game

All the money raised from the DLCs will be spent toward the game, we take none of it for personal use

We will add more DLCs over time, but we also want DLCs to have something interesting
For instance, extra Artworks, Music, etc...

We've noticed a few people bought it and refunded it not long after,
If you wish to get the content of the DLCs without paying, just feel free to ask, we have no issue giving it away. 

[h1]Long Story Short[/h1]
We've made DLCs to help accelerate the development of the game
The money will allow us to afford paying some people to help us
if you wish to support the development of the game, we would appreciate you buy the DLCs
We also promise we will never hide content behind a pay wall. so the DLCs will always remain an optional thing

notes.title: Ships
notes.content:
[h1]Missing Ships![/h1]
We had a lot of people who had an issue with the ships folder
It seems the game didn't extracted the ships properly which resulted with an empty folder

This is why we have made this little update.
Now, the ships folder is included in the main directory of the game
To find it, simply follow these simple instructions:
[olist]
[*]Right click on the game in your steam library
[*]Click on Proprieties
[*]Click on the "local Files" tab
[*]Click on "browse local files"
[/olist]

This will open the game's directory and you should be able to find a "Ships" folder
I suggest you copy the ships from that folder into the one generated by the game
It will be a simple way to load the ships

notes.title: Hotfix 1: Crashing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35944196/c7e335ae69b3adcc64d8af2cea2ed188c219d94a.png[/img]

Relentless crashing has caused a lot of frustration among the community, sorry about that.
We hadn't planned for such a massive influx of new players upon launch, which just worsened the situation.

We have isolated the cause of the issue in the GUI framework we used, and have replaced it completely with an alternative.

The new version should be far more stable.
